recipes.name: Killed Lettuce and Onion
ingredients_raw: 1 head leaf lettuce - rinsed, dried and torn into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned and crisp, about 10 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble; set aside.
Add green onions to bacon grease; cook and stir until onions reach desired tenderness, about 1 minute. Pour onions and bacon grease over lettuce; toss lightly. Top with crumbled bacon and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Killed Lettuce and Onion
raw_recipe.description: Killed lettuce (aka kilt lettuce) is a traditional Appalachian recipe featuring fresh leaf lettuce tossed with hot grease, green onion, and crumbled bacon.

review.reviewBody: I grew up with a different version of this recipe and we still enjoy it. First of all it's much easier to cut the bacon into small pieces before you fry it. It takes less time and cooks evenly. I don't toss my onions in the bacon grease, just sprinkle them over the salad before adding the hot dressing. I only use about 2 Tbsp. of the bacon fat and add about 1/4 apple cider vinegar, ground black pepper and sugar (to taste, we like it pretty sweet). Heat until the sugar dissolves in the vinegar and bacon fat. Pour hot mixture over the greens and enjoy. It's less fat and gives it a little bite from the vinegar although it does add sugar to the mix. It's delicious.

I grew up in Southern Missouri where we always ate "Wilted" lettuce...had the same ingredients, but you heat the bacon grease to a very hot temperature in the skillet and add about 1/4 cup water with a little sugar and some vinegar to the hot grease, then pour over the lettuce and onion. The liquid makes it more like a hot bacon salad dressing! Yummy!

My family (Eastern Kentucky by way of Germany) called this Wilted Lettuce. I agree with the others who have said that it needs some apple cider vinegar and a touch of granulated sugar cooked with the bacon grease before you pour it over the lettuce. When I was growing up and our garden was producing a ton of leaf lettuce, we'd eat this for dinner. I still love it!

My family calls it wilted lettuce. I use only about 2-3 tbsp. of the bacon grease and add about 2 tbsp. of cider vinegar. Sometimes I also add 1-2 teaspoons of sugar, if I am in the mood for a sweet & sour flavor. Also, as Spinmom suggests, it’s easier to chop up the bacon before cooking instead of after

Grew up in SW Pennsylvania at the base of the Appalachian mountains and we called this "wilted" lettuce. Similar, but we used bacon grease instead on "bacon." We cut onions, added apple cider vinegar, sugar and salt along with the bacon grease and cooked it until the onions were tender and immediately poured it on top of the lettuce or any other greens for that matter. I have even had it with dandelion leaves. Delicious!

After some tweaking, this recipe turned out great! It's the kind of thing that is made from tradition, so everyone has their individual likes. My family called this wilted lettuce (Arkansas).
I made it as my mother did. I put the lettuce in a bowl and added raw green onion and a little bit of raw radish, cooked the bacon and let it drain. With the bacon fat still in the pan I added some apple cider vinegar and a little sugar, and got that real hot. I poured it over the lettuce and stuff, covered the bowl with the pan (upside down on the bowl), and let it sit a minute. Afterwards, I added the crumpled up bacon and stirred. It ends up being kind of sweet and sour. Mom and I used to make a meal out of this - we didn't need anything else. I've wanted to make this for a long time, but didn't remember how until I saw your recipe, and I thank you for that...

I grew up in Western NC (Wilkes County) and it was called wilted lettuce(well, just about any greens, with mustard greens being my fav) . The bacon grease was rocket hot to the point of the first wisp of smoke, and vinegar was definitely a component.

This is a summer favorite of my family. We all anxiously await the fresh lettuce from the garden to make this once a year treat. I make it a little differently, I don't cook the onion, and only add enough hot grease to lightly coat the lettuce (about 2 tablespoons). I also add a fair amount of salt, my friends, neighbors and family LOVE this!

I grew up in Tenn and my grandmother made this all the time. We ate ours with white bread. You definitely have to add salt and pepper. I just cut up the bacon, fry it, and pour directly over the lettuce and onions. Its so good.
Good old fashioned recipe like my papaw used to make. Eastern KY. I sometimes add vinegar and a spoonful of sugar but not every time. So good with cornbread.

I am so happy to see this recipe. I haven't made this in years and had forgotten about it. I'll never forget the look on my new husband's face (back in the 60's) when I told him what I was cooking for dinner. He ended up loving it and requesting it often. I was taught to use leaf lettuce and added just a little vinegar to the dressing along with salt and pepper. Guess what I'm fixing tonight???

The recipe I grew up with was more like Spinmom's. We just called it wilted lettuce though. I only remember it being made in the late spring/early summer when we had lettuce fresh from the garden. People really can't believe how good it is, until they actually try it!
We in Wisconsin,call it Wilted Lettuce. It's a German thing.
My family has made this for over 60 years. You need to add vinegar and salt before adding the hot bacon grease. We also crumble some bacon in it. It’s really delicious if you fix it correctly.
I had never heard of this til I moved WNC and a friend had us over for a "real" NC dinner. This is one of the best salads I have ever eaten.
Very good basic recipe for this old fashion favorite! I recommend this recipe for the beginner to an expert!
We loved this, it turned out great!
Just the way my family made it. Not exactly healthy, but oh so good.
Growing up we just called it lettuce and onions. Also, we always added vinegar, I can't imagine eating it without.
I always thought it was called wilted lettuce. I have had this myself and is very good.
